content.text: {"headline":"Approve P3 (overtime + chat deflection + break delays + callbacks) for 12:00-14:00, and bring in the duty manager: it is the best available plan, but at 57.7% it still falls well short of the 80% target.","why":"Calls on general are running long because CRM customer search is taking 20–40 seconds (P2 incident INC-20261021-5862, opened 09:55). Handle time reached 646 s at 10:00 against about 350–376 s forecast, while volume and staffing are close to plan. Service level fell to 14.7% with 18 abandons in that interval. If we do nothing, 12:00-14:00 is predicted at 30.6% with 22.9% abandons. P3 offers overtime to 20 general and 12 payments agents from 12:30-14:30, delays breaks, adds IVR callback and 20% chat deflection on both queues. It lifts the window to 57.7% (general 59.2%, payments 56.6%), cuts abandons to 12.0% and raises rest-of-day to 85.7%, for ₹7,884. No plan reaches 80%. ESCALATION: P3 is below the 70% escalation line (ESC-02), so the duty manager should be involved, both to approve and to push for faster resolution of the CRM incident, which is the real fix.","trade_offs":["R1 and R2 cost the same ₹7,884 and avoid break delays, but predict lower service: R1 56.9% (general only 53.3%) and R2 51.6%, with higher abandons (13.3% and 15.1%).","P4 is cheaper at ₹6,480 but reaches only 41.1% with 15.9% abandons.","P2 costs just ₹1,404 but reaches only 38.5%.","P1 is free but makes things worse than doing nothing (20.8%, general 10.9%).","P3 balances both queues, with neither queue left far behind."],"watch":"Watch CRM search times and the incident status. If the slowness clears before 12:00, scale back the overtime. Also watch overtime take-up on both queues: P3's prediction assumes the 20 general and 12 payments agents accept. Track general handle time against the roughly 646 s seen at 10:00."}
